name: Gongduk
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Karma Tshering (University of Sydney). 2015. Documentation of the flora and fauna of Gongduk. ELAR deposit dk0353 (ELDP project 2013)
sources.note: Deposit page (read via direct download; saved HTML is the Preservica challenge page) states 'a phonological analysis and grammatical sketch of the language has also been produced' and that a phonemic orthography was developed; the analysis itself was not found online (Sydney repository blocked; no Crossref/DataCite record).

sources.citation: Gerber, Pascal. 2022. Verb stem alternation in Gongduk: Synchronic and diachronic analysis. Language and Linguistics 23(2): 240-273. doi:10.1075/lali.00105.ger (CC BY 4.0)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Nothing. Sections 2-3 give phonotactics (allowed codas /p t k/, nasals, /r/, /ʔ/; no clusters; verbs almost all monosyllabic) and morphophonology; the words stress, accent, tone, pitch never occur (only 'prosodic status' of a reconstructed suffix, p. 266).

sources.citation: Gerber, Pascal. 2018. Areal features in Gongduk, Bjokapakha and Black Mountain Mönpa phonology (Draft, 4 May 2018), Universität Bern; draft of Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 43(1): 55-86 (2020)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about Gongduk stress or accent. Whole paper is segmental: dental fricatives, dental affricates, central vowel /ɤ/, glottalisation of final stops, uvular plosives, velar-nasal nasalisation. Only prosodic remark is fn. 35 that Black Mountain Mönpa has two register tones (Hyslop 2016b; van Driem 1995: 235); no tone or stress claim for Gongduk.
